symptom: Every settings write (alter settings runtime/language, mxcli test's after-startup microflow) failed with 'element id(s) are used more than once … held by [Settings$ServerConfiguration Settings$ServerConfiguration]' on a project with two server configurations named 'Default' (a merge brings them in; Studio Pro and mx check accept it).
cause: settingsoverlay.Configurations paired each modelled configuration with its stored document through a map keyed on the lower-cased name, so the second stored document overwrote the first in the map and both modelled configurations were overlaid onto it: the unit held its $ID twice and the duplicate-id guard refused the write.
fix: Pair by stored $ID first (the read path sets ServerConfiguration.ID), then by name among unclaimed documents, each stored document claimed at most once. The executor's name lookup (alter settings configuration, the constant override, drop configuration, create or modify) refuses a name more than one configuration has, instead of acting on the first.
insight: A name-keyed map is a silent dedupe: the last entry wins and nothing errors until the identity guard downstream. Any overlay that pairs model elements with stored ones should pair on $ID when the model carries one, and treat names as an addressing convenience that can be ambiguous. WorkflowGroups and Languages use the same byName/byCode shape; their keys are unique in Studio Pro today.
